speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for seeing me; I understand you are experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues. To better understand your condition, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if they are worsening over time?

Also, have you noticed any other changes, such as changes in your sense of smell, sleep patterns, or difficulties with buttoning your shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the 70-year-old male has a one-year history of progressive left-sided resting tremor and recent memory impairment affecting daily tasks like paying bills. Given the asymmetry of the tremor and cognitive decline, could you clarify if he experiences stiffness or slowness of movement, and whether he has any history of similar conditions in his family?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease with Dementia (PDD)

The combination of a progressive, asymmetric resting tremor, bradykinesia (soft speech, reduced facial expression), and early cognitive decline affecting instrumental activities of daily living is highly suggestive of Parkinson's Disease with Dementia. Given the one-year history of motor symptoms followed by cognitive issues, this presentation aligns with PDD rather than Dementia with Lewy Bodies. Have you noticed any episodes of hallucinations, visual disturbances, or sudden drops in blood pressure when standing?
